Кто‑то однажды сказал: «Когда живёт надежда, ночь становится менее тёмной, одиночество — менее глубоким, а страх — менее острым». Когда я работал помощником капеллана в тюрьме, я сидел с осуждёнными и слушал, как они говорили о своей беде. Почти без исключения все говорили о надежде однажды выйти на свободу. Даже если у них был пожизненный срок, они надеялись выйти.

Я разговаривал с людьми, которые не признаются, что рождены свыше, но всё же надеются попасть в небо. Эти люди не смеют прекратить надеяться. Их надежда основана на их собственной надежде! Такая надежда — скудная пища, без сомнения. Эта мысль напоминает мне слова Иисуса в Иоанна 10:1–2 о входе в овчарню. «Но который входит дверью, тот и пастырь овец». Люди строят свою надежду на небе на многих шатких основаниях. Кто‑то основывает надежду на том, что был крещён в определённой церкви. Кто‑то надеется на своё церковное членство. Некоторые надеются на свои добрые дела, другие — надеются на собственную надежду. Однако Библия говорит: «...если кто не родится свыше, не может увидеть Царства Божия» (Иоанна 3:3).

Существует истинная надежда и ложная надежда. Ложная надежда — это «взбираться другим путём», а истинная надежда — это «тот, кто входит дверью».

«Ибо мы спасены надеждою; но надежда, увиденная, уже не есть надежда; ибо кто видит, чего ещё надеется?» (Римлянам 8:24). Слово «надежда» здесь означает «с ожиданием или с великой надеждой». Можем ли мы сказать, что мы спасены великой надеждой? Да, можем. «Не трудитесь за тленную пищу, но за ту пищу, которая остаётся в вечную жизнь, которую Сын Человеческий даст вам; ибо Его запечатал Бог Отец» (Иоанна 6:27). Это кажется некоторым родом противоречия. Разве мы не спасены по благодати? Да, мы спасены благодатью через веру (Ефесянам 2:8). Тогда что значит быть спасённым надеждой и трудиться за «пищу, которая остаётся в вечную жизнь»?

«Тогда они сказали Ему: что нам делать, чтобы творить дела Божии? Иисус ответил им: это — дело Божие, чтобы веровать в Того, Кого Он послал» (Иоанна 6:28–29). Только по благодати мы спасаемся, но, как показывает этот отрывок, благодать ставит условие. Условие благодати — веровать в Него. Ещё одно условие спасения — покаяние (Марк 1:15), а также несение креста. «Если кто хочет идти за Мною, отвергнись себя, и возьми крест свой, и следуй за Мною» (Марк 8:34).

Всё, что мы делаем для Христа — будь то вера, покаяние или ношение креста — происходит по благодати. Всё, что у нас есть или что мы делаем, — из‑за Него. Мы не трудимся ради нашего спасения, потому что Сам Христос сказал: «Совершилось». У нас нет надежды, если мы не выполняем условия нашего спасения. Как только мы принимаем Господа Иисуса как Спасителя, тогда «надежда не постыжает» (Римлянам 5:5).

Когда Христос оживает в нас, мы любим Его и выбираем слушаться Его. Иисус становится для нас дороже по мере того, как мы созреваем в христианской жизни. По мере роста наших взаимоотношений растёт и наше ожидание. Чем больше мы познаём Его, тем сильнее мы стремимся быть в Его присутствии. По мере возрастания нашего предвкушения увидеть Его мы стараемся делать всё возможное, чтобы угодить Ему. Наше большое рвение не даёт нам утомиться, таким образом «мы спасаемся надеждою».

Ваша надежда похожа на ту, кто «взбирается другим путём», или на ту, «кто входит дверью»? Есть ли у вашей надежды основание, или это пустая надежда без фундамента?

Надюсь, вы возрастаете «...в Нём во всём, который есть глава, Христос» (Ефесянам 4:15).

Надеюсь, вы могли бы ещё немного возрасти, чтобы ваше ожидание увидеть Христа тоже увеличилось. Свидетельство об этом ожидания: «...в том и стону, томясь желанием облечься в дом наш, который от небес» (2 Коринфянам 5:2).

The message was brief. “Dr. Waldron, would you call Mrs. Jones back about her labs?”

I was puzzled. I didn’t remember ordering any labs for Mrs. Jones. As far as I could remember, she was seeing a specialist and just had surgery for colon cancer. Maybe they had ordered the labs. But if so, they certainly should have followed up on them.

I opened the chart and looked in the lab section. Quickly my eye went to my patient’s kidney function and stopped. Her kidney function had declined a huge amount in the last week.

I called her and then her kidney specialist. Over the next half hour, her situation came into view. Because of her colon surgery, she was losing a lot of fluid, enough that she couldn’t keep up. This, in turn, was making her kidney function a lot worse, along with dropping her potassium level.

To take care of it, she would need IV fluids – once or twice a week – to keep up with the fluids she was losing. Without that, her kidneys would shut down completely.

In a sense, Mrs. Jones was dealing with kidney burnout—a situation where they were putting out more than they were taking in and suffering as a result.

As I was thinking about this, my mind went to the Dead Sea. The Dead Sea is “Dead” because it has such a high level of minerals and salts that very few, other than a few microorganisms, can survive.

The reason for this is that the Dead Sea has no outlet. The Jordan River drains into it, carrying fresh water, and then sits in a basin. Some of the water evaporates, and what remains are the salts and minerals in the water.

Over the thousands of years since the fall of Sodom and Gomorrah, this inland body of water has become one of the saltiest places on earth. It is a body of water that is neither useful for irrigation nor a place where plants and animals can thrive.

Neither situation is healthy, yet this is exactly how most people live their lives, typically gravitating towards one pole or the other. Either they fill their schedule to the maximum, leaving no time for quiet reflection, or they resist any efforts to get them to invest their time and talents and avoid these sorts of activities.

I want to spend a little time thinking about burnout. What causes it, and how we can avoid it?

Everyone has Limits

I Samuel 30 tells the story of David returning to Ziklag. Upon his arrival, he discovered, to his dismay, that the Amalekites had invaded Philistine territory, burned the town, and taken captive all the people who were present.

David and his men had been gone three days and were already tired from their journey to and from Aphek, where King Agag had mustered his forces. Despite this and their anguish at the loss of their family members and material possessions, David consulted God and decided to pursue to the Amalekites out into the desert.

They had only gone as far as the Brook Besor when a third of his men gave up. Scripture tells us they were “too faint” to cross the brook. They were physically and mentally exhausted. Even if they had been able to hold things together for another day, they would be useless in battle.

So it was that David left them behind and continued to pursue the Amalekites, eventually defeating them with the four hundred men who were able to persevere. Here, we come to the interesting part. The men who had won the victory looked down on the men who had been faint. They said those faint-hearted men could have their families back, but all the spoil would be reserved for those who had won the victory.

In response, David said, “Ye shall not do so, my brethren, with that which the Lord hath given us, who hath preserved us, and delivered the company that came against us into our hand. For who will hearken unto you in this matter? but as his part is that goeth down to the battle, so shall his part be that tarrieth by the stuff: they shall part alike.” (I Samuel 30:23,24)

David did not wish to penalize those who had tried but did not have the strength to make it through to the final battle.

Perhaps this speaks of the grace we ought to extend to others who don’t have the strength or energy to continue for a season. Maybe it lets us know that we should extend that same grace to ourselves.

What is Burnout?

There are different definitions for burnout, but it all comes down to a state of physical, mental, or emotional exhaustion related to too much stress over an extended period of time. We tend to think of this stress as work-related. There are too many projects going on at once, not enough help, or an employer who has high expectations.

Stress is stress, and it all adds up. Even if work isn’t stressful, if you have a newborn baby at home, a family member with dementia, or many church responsibilities, you can still reach the place where you have little left to give.

It is as though you are in a vehicle traveling 90 mph, and you push the accelerator a little harder, and nothing happens. In response, you push the gas pedal even harder, and a screeching noise comes from the engine. Suddenly, the dashboard lights up with funny lights, and the car starts to slow down.

The question is, how can we avoid burnout and what should we do if we realize that we are heading towards it?

Understanding Burnout

Burnout leads to both physical and emotional depletion. The problem with burnout is that even if a particular stressor causes it – say, a situation at work or a family health problem – it will affect numerous other relationships.

People dealing with burnout often exhibit symptoms consistent with depression and anxiety. They may become withdrawn, lack motivation to be involved with church and family activities, or get angry quicker than people who are not dealing with burnout.

There is even a suggestion that burnout can lead to the weakening of our immune systems. This could lead to more colds and viral infections.

Identify Early Signs

We need to know ourselves. There are signs that other people can see in our lives and how we relate to others that we don’t necessarily identify as a problem.

People who are on the edge of burnout feel hopeless. They may hide it from their coworkers, but often, their family members realize that something is wrong. You used to have a sunny disposition, and now you are discouraged, not only about the present but also the future.

You might lack motivation and have low energy levels. In a sense, you are going through the motions and just doing enough to get by – both at work and in your home. This is likely related to your feelings of hopelessness.

You may find that you are more irritable than you used to be. Little things bother or aggravate you, and you find yourself smothering angry retorts.

It is important to realize that you are heading down this road for several reasons. First, you are not the only one who suffers when you are burned out. Your family must deal with you and your “grumpiness.” Also, the longer you go without taking care of things, the harder it is to get back to a place of balance.

As a physician, I see people all the time who “didn’t have time” to get something taken care of until they could no longer ignore it. At this point, it will take a major procedure to set things right. It would have been easier to correct if they came in with the first symptom.

Make a Priority List

Everything in our life has a priority level. People who do not prioritize end up feeling scattered as they try to do everything at once. This is a recipe for disaster. To me, it makes sense to divide our tasks into four buckets:

  1. Things that need to be done relatively quickly
  2. Things that need to be done but can wait a bit
  3. Things that we’d like to do, but don’t need to
  4. Things that we should let go of.

Here might be a good place to mention that just because something needs to be done does not mean you need to do it. Sometimes, someone in your home or workplace could help with one of the tasks on your to-do list.

Once we have made our priority list, we need to do something about it. If you simply assign a priority to everything in your life but continue to try to do everything, it won’t help your situation at all.

The point of this exercise is to figure out what things you can eliminate from your schedule, so you have more space to breathe.

Make First Things First

One of the things that happens when we are overwhelmed is that we stop doing self-care. We grab unhealthy food on the go, stop spending time in prayer and devotions, and quit exercising.

Doing these things takes time, and that is exactly what we think we don’t have when we are living on the margins of our energy. Self-care is extremely important but often gets assigned a priority of zero and is seldom included in a day’s activity.

As we begin to replenish our spiritual nourishment, we must also make sure we take care of our physical health.

Take Time Apart

After feeding the multitudes, Mark 6:46 tells of Jesus, “And when he had sent them away, he departed into a mountain to pray.” Even Jesus had times when He needed to be alone without distractions.

It is easy to focus on the prayer aspect of this passage, and that is important, but let's focus on the solitary aspect of this experience. Jesus even left His closest followers behind during this time of seeking God’s face.

There are times when we need to escape from the pressure of human interactions and find a peaceful place where we can be alone.

Put Down Technology

Part of making rest time truly restful is to eliminate sources of distraction. Phones and electronic tablets are exactly the types of things that can keep our minds from achieving the peace (shalom) that we both desire and need.

Digital burnout is a new term that is being used to describe people who feel apathetic and exhausted from spending hours each day staring at screens. Many workers spend seven or eight hours a day looking at computer screens and then get even more screen time after work.

The funny thing is that the most productive workers are often people who use old-fashioned things like paper calendars and leave phones out of meetings. As wonderful as phones are, they are also immensely distracting for most of us.

So often, we have time away that is simply not restful. The reason is that we continue to receive texts and emails and can still access social media. If you are not someone who can put his phone away and ignore it (it takes a lot of willpower to do this), then leave your phone in another room and create some distance. This will seem stressful, but we can focus on recharging ourselves by creating a screen-free zone.

Build Breaks into Your Day

There is a certain amount of work that must be done each day, and it often feels like too much for the allotted 24 hours. There is certainly no time to stop, stretch, and take a five-minute walk, or at least that's what we tell ourselves.

In reality, if you take a five-minute break every few hours to do something non-work related, you will come back refreshed and more ready to deal with the problems of the day.

Do something healthy during this time. Take a short walk or eat an apple. Chowing down a bag of potato chips or eating a couple candy bars is not likely to produce the desired results.

The problem is often with our own expectations. People who struggle with burnout often have extremely high personal standards and get frustrated when they not measure up to that standard.

Be Intentional about Rest

One of the messages of the Old Testament was the importance of the Sabbath. I have heard many people argue that in the New Testament period, we no longer need to practice the Sabbath. Didn’t Paul say that one day was like the other? Didn’t Jesus defend His disciples for picking grain on the Sabbath?

Regardless of what you believe about the importance of keeping the Sabbath, it is still important that we take time to rest. This is the real message that Jesus was conveying when He said that the “Sabbath was created for man, not man for the Sabbath” (Mark 2:27).

Rest is not simply sleeping till 10 am and then doing nothing. Rest is actively making decisions that will help us recharge our depleted batteries. Go out for breakfast with a friend, take a hike, or take a good book and go somewhere without cell service and focus on something other than situations that are depleting you.

Jesus understood the human need for rest, this is why He told His disciples “Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while” (Mark 6:31). This time of rest would give them energy for their next time of ministry.

Don’t Buy into Myths

People tell themselves all sorts of lies that can lead to pushing themselves too hard. I’ll list a few of them and some thoughts about each one.

“I’m the only one who can do this task.” This feels true. The other people in our home or workplace are not helping us the way we wish that they would. Sometimes, it simply feels easier to do the task ourselves rather than spend time teaching someone else how to do it. We need to remember that if we died, the people around us would figure out how to get things done. We can assign them some of the tasks today before we die.

“If I just get this job done today, tomorrow will be easier.” I hate to be the bearer of bad news, but each day has 24 hours, and somehow, they always get filled up. I have given up the idea that there is a time in my life coming up soon that will have nothing on the schedule. If a rest comes, it will come because I have made an effort to clear my schedule, not because by some random occurrence, one day, I happen to not have a single task in it.

“God will never give me more than I can handle.” God has promised many things. He has promised that when there is a temptation, He will give us an opportunity to escape it (I Corinthians 10:13). He has also promised that He will never leave us or forsake us (Hebrews 13:5). I do not read anywhere in Scripture that God will keep us from overfilling our lives. He has simply promised that He will give us opportunity to take a different path and will walk beside us on our way.

So often the heavy load we carry is because other people, or even we, ourselves, have put too many things on our task list. Suppose I choose to put too many patients on my schedule and I am feeling exhausted. In that case, it is time for me to take responsibility for what I have done, rather than claiming a mythical promise that God will keep me from overwhelming myself.

“These are all good things that I am doing.” Doctors face this a lot. We want to squeeze one more patient into the schedule and stay just a little later to answer another message because we feel responsible. We hate to think that someone might need to go to the Emergency Department because we did not take care of them when they needed help.

Just because the things in your schedule are “good things” that benefit other people and are building the kingdom, does not mean that you don’t need to cut back in one area or another. If you are feeling emotionally depleted, it is probably time to remove a few items from your to-do list.

Conclusion

There are other things that could be mentioned. Getting support from someone else, meditating on Scripture, and even taking a vacation are all things that can help.

When I read about some of the famous preachers of the past, I see in some of their lives a roller coaster. They pushed themselves to the max, got involved in large numbers of projects, and then had an emotional breakdown. They would take some time off and, a month or two later, launch back into the same activities. This cycle continued for their whole ministry.

Jesus tells us that His yoke is easy, and His burden is light (Matt, 11:28-30). If we are at the point of exhaustion, we need to consider whether we have Jesus’ yoke or if we are laboring under the burden of our own creation.

Jesus knows our limitations. He wants us to have balance, living in such a way that we not only have strength for today but also for tomorrow, next week, and next year – till He comes again.

پیغام مختصر تھا۔ “ڈاکٹر والڈرن، کیا آپ مسز جونز کو ان کے لیبارٹری کے نتائج بارے واپس کال کر دیں گے؟”

میں حیران رہ گیا۔ مجھے یاد نہیں تھا کہ میں نے مسز جونز کے لیے کوئی لیب ٹیسٹ لکھوائے ہوں۔ جہاں تک مجھے یاد تھا، وہ ایک ماہر کے پاس جا رہی تھیں اور حال ہی میں کولن کینسر کی سرجری کروائی تھی۔ شاید اُنہوں نے ٹیسٹ آرڈر کیے تھے۔ لیکن اگر ایسا تھا تو انہیں یقیناً اُن کے نتائج پر فالو اپ کرنا چاہیے تھا۔

میں نے چارٹ کھولا اور لیب سیکشن میں دیکھا۔ میری نظر تیزی سے مریضہ کے گردے کے فنکشن کی طرف گئی اور رک گئی۔ پچھلے ہفتے کے دوران اس کی گردے کی کارکردگی بہت حد تک خراب ہو گئی تھی۔

میں نے اسے فون کیا اور پھر اس کے گردوں کے ماہر کو بھی۔ اگلے پچیس تیس منٹ میں، اس کی صورتِ حال واضح ہو گئی۔ کولن کی سرجری کی وجہ سے وہ بہت زیادہ سیال کھو رہی تھی، اتنا کہ وہ اسے پورا نہیں کر پارہی تھی۔ اس کے نتیجے میں اس کی گردوں کی کارکردگی بہت خراب ہو رہی تھی اور اس کا پوٹاشیم لیول بھی گر رہا تھا۔

اس کا علاج کرنے کے لیے، اسے وریدی مائعات (IV fluids) کی ضرورت ہوگی — ہفتے میں ایک یا دو بار — تاکہ وہ گم ہونے والے سیالات کو پورا رکھ سکے۔ اگر ایسا نہ ہوا تو اس کے گردے مکمل طور پر بند ہو جائیں گے۔

ایک معنی میں، مسز جونز گردے کے “برباد ہونے” سے دوچار تھیں — ایسی حالت جہاں وہ زیادہ کھو رہی تھیں بنسبت جو وہ حاصل کر رہی تھیں اور اس کا برا نتیجہ نکلا۔

جب میں اس کے بارے میں سوچ رہا تھا تو میرا ذہن مردہ سمندر کی طرف گیا۔ مردہ سمندر ‘‘مردہ’’ اس لیے ہے کہ اس میں نمکیات اور معدنیات کی سطح اتنی زیادہ ہے کہ چند خوردبینی جانداروں کے علاوہ بہت کم ہی زندہ رہ سکتے ہیں۔

اس کی وجہ یہ ہے کہ مردہ سمندر کا کوئی راستہ باہر نہیں ہے۔ دریائے اردن اس میں تازہ پانی لے کر آتا ہے، اور پھر وہ ایک کھائی میں بیٹھ جاتا ہے۔ کچھ پانی بخارات بن کر ختم ہو جاتا ہے، اور جو باقی رہتا ہے وہ پانی میں موجود نمکیات اور معدنیات ہیں۔

سومو اور گمورہ کے زوال کے ہزاروں سالوں میں، یہ اندرونی پانی کا وسیلہ زمین کے سب سے نمکین مقامات میں سے ایک بن گیا ہے۔ یہ وہ پانی ہے جو نہ تو آبپاشی کے کام آتا ہے اور نہ ہی پودے اور جانور اس میں پھل پھول سکتے ہیں۔

یہ دونوں حالتیں صحت مند نہیں ہیں، پھر بھی یہی طریقۂِ زندگی زیادہ تر لوگ اپنائے رکھتے ہیں، عموماً ایک قطب یا دوسرے کی طرف مائل رہتے ہیں۔ یا تو وہ اپنا شیڈول حدِ عظم تک بھر دیتے ہیں، اور خاموش غور و فکر کے لیے کوئی وقت نہیں چھوڑتے، یا وہ اپنی مہارت اور وقت لگانے کی کسی کوشش کو رد کر دیتے ہیں اور ایسی سرگرمیوں سے بچتے رہتے ہیں۔

میں تھوڑا وقت خرچ کرنا چاہتا ہوں تاکہ بَرنا آؤٹ (burnout) کے بارے میں سوچیں۔ اس کی وجہ کیا ہے، اور ہم اسے کیسے بچ سکتے ہیں؟

ہر کسی کی حدیں ہیں

پہلا سموئیل باب 30 میں داؤد کی زِیکلاگ واپسی کا قصہ بیان ہے۔ اپنی آمد پر اس نے مایوسی کے ساتھ دیکھا کہ عمالیکوں نے فِلِسطینی علاقے پر حملہ کیا تھا، قصبہ جلا دیا تھا، اور وہاں موجود تمام لوگوں کو قیدی بنا لیا تھا۔

داؤد اور اس کے مرد تین دن غائب رہے تھے اور پہلے ہی اپھیک کے سفر کے باعث تھکے ہوئے تھے، جہاں بادشاہ آگاغ نے اپنی فوجیں جمع کی تھیں۔ اس سب اور اپنے اہل خانہ اور مادی املاک کے نقصان کی تکلیف کے باوجود، داؤد نے خدا سے مشورہ کیا اور عمالیکیوں کا پیچھا کرنے کا فیصلہ کیا۔

وہ بس برس بیصر تک گئے تھے جب اس کے ایک تہائی مرد ہار مان گئے۔ صحیفہ ہمیں بتاتی ہے کہ وہ ‘‘بہت کمزور’’ ہو گئے تھے کہ وہ ندی پار نہ کر سکے۔ وہ جسمانی اور دماغی طور پر تھکے ہوئے تھے۔ اگرچہ وہ ایک اور دن کے لیے حالات سنبھال لیتے، تب بھی وہ جنگ میں کارآمد نہ رہتے۔

یوں داؤد نے انہیں پیچھے چھوڑ دیا اور عمالیکیوں کا پیچھا جاری رکھا، آخر کار چار سؤ مردوں کے ساتھ جو استقامت برقرار رکھنے کے قابل تھے، انہیں شکست دی۔ یہاں ہم دلچسپ حصہ پر پہنچتے ہیں۔ جو مرد فتح حاصل کرنے والے تھے انہوں نے کمزور پڑنے والے مردوں کو حقارت کی نگاہ سے دیکھا۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ جو کم حوصلہ مرد ہیں وہ اپنے خاندان واپس پا سکتے ہیں، مگر سب لُوٹ صرف ان کے لیے محفوظ رکھی جائے جو فتح کے مستحق تھے۔

جواب میں داؤد نے کہا، “تم ایسا نہ کرو، اے میرے بھائیو، اُس چیز کے ساتھ جو خدا نے ہمیں دی ہے، جو ہمیں حفظ کیا اور اُس قوم کو جو ہمارے خلاف آئی تھی ہمارے ہاتھ میں دے دیا۔ کون تمہاری بات سنے گا اس معاملے میں؟ بلکہ جیسا حصہ اُس کا ہے جو جنگ میں اترا، ویسا ہی حصہ اُس کا ہوگا جو سامان کے پاس ٹھہرا رہے گا: وہ برابر برابر حصہ لیں گے۔” (پہلا سموئیل 30:23،24)

داؤد ایسی سزا نہیں دینا چاہتا تھا ان لوگوں کو جنہوں نے کوشش کی مگر آخر تک پہنچنے کی طاقت نہیں رکھی۔

شاید یہ ہمیں اُس رحمت کی طرف اشارہ کرتا ہے جو ہمیں دوسروں کو دینی چاہیے جو ایک موسم کے لیے طاقت یا توانائی نہیں رکھتے۔ ممکن ہے یہ ہمیں بتاتا ہو کہ ہمیں اپنے لیے بھی وہی رحم دِل ہونا چاہیے۔

بَرنا آؤٹ کیا ہے؟

بَرنا آؤٹ کی مختلف تعریفیں ہیں، مگر یہ سب کسی طویل عرصے تک زیادہ دباؤ کے نتیجے میں جسمانی، ذہنی، یا جذباتی تھکن کی حالت پر آکر ختم ہوتا ہے۔ ہم اس دباؤ کو عموماً کام سے متعلق سمجھتے ہیں۔ بہت سی منصوبہ بندیاں ایک ساتھ چل رہی ہیں، مدد کم ہے، یا مالک کے غیر حقیقی توقعات ہیں۔

دباؤ تو دباؤ ہی ہے، اور یہ سب جمع ہوتا ہے۔ چاہے کام دباؤ کا باعث نہ بھی ہو، اگر آپ کے گھر میں نوزائیدہ بچہ ہو، خاندان کا کوئی رکن دماغی افت کے ساتھ ہو، یا آپ کے پاس چرچ کی بہت سی ذمہ داریاں ہوں، پھر بھی آپ اُس مقام تک پہنچ سکتے ہیں جہاں دینے کے لیے بہت کم بچتا ہے۔

یہ ایسا ہے جیسے آپ گاڑی میں 90 میل فی گھنٹہ سے سفر کر رہے ہوں، اور آپ تھوڑا مزید رفتار بڑھاتے ہیں، مگر کچھ نہیں ہوتا۔ اس کے جواب میں آپ ایندھن پیڈل اور زور سے دباتے ہیں، اور انجِن سے ایک چیختی ہوئی آواز آتی ہے۔ اچانک ڈیش بورڈ پر عجیب علامتیں جل اٹھتی ہیں اور گاڑی سُست ہونے لگتی ہے۔

سوال یہ ہے کہ ہم برن آؤٹ سے کیسے بچ سکتے ہیں اور اگر ہمیں محسوس ہو کہ ہم اس کی طرف جا رہے ہیں تو ہمیں کیا کرنا چاہیے؟

برن آؤٹ کو سمجھنا

برن آؤٹ جسمانی اور جذباتی دونوں طرح کی کمی کی طرف لے جاتا ہے۔ مسئلہ یہ ہے کہ چاہے کوئی مخصوص دباؤ—مثلاً کام کی صورتِ حال یا خاندان کی صحت کا مسئلہ—اس کا سبب بنے، یہ کئی دوسرے رشتوں پر اثر انداز ہوتا ہے۔

برن آؤٹ سے دوچار لوگ عموماً ڈپریشن اور اضطراب سے مطابقت رکھنے والے علامات دکھاتے ہیں۔ وہ الگ تھلگ ہو سکتے ہیں، چرچ اور خاندانی سرگرمیوں میں حصہ لینے کی حوصلہ شکنی محسوس کر سکتے ہیں، یا اُن کا غصہ اُن لوگوں سے جلدی پھٹ سکتا ہے جو برن آؤٹ میں نہیں ہیں۔

یہ بھی مشورہ دیا جاتا ہے کہ برن آؤٹ ہماری مدافعتی نظام کو کمزور کر سکتا ہے۔ اس سے زیادہ زکام اور وائرل انفیکشنز ہو سکتے ہیں۔

ابتدائی نشانیاں شناخت کریں

ہمیں خود کو جاننا چاہیے۔ ایسی نشانیاں ہیں جو دوسرے لوگ ہماری زندگی میں اور دوسروں کے ساتھ ہمارے تعلقات میں دیکھ سکتے ہیں جنہیں ہم لازمی طور پر مسئلہ سمجھتے نہیں۔

جو لوگ برن آؤٹ کے کنارے پر ہوتے ہیں وہ بے امید محسوس کرتے ہیں۔ وہ اپنے ساتھی کار کارکنوں سے اسے چھپا سکتے ہیں، مگر اکثر اُن کے خاندان کے اراکین محسوس کر لیتے ہیں کہ کچھ غلط ہے۔ آپ پہلے خوش مزاج تھے، اور اب آپ مایوس ہیں، نہ صرف حال کے بارے میں بلکہ مستقبل کے بارے میں بھی۔

آپ میں حوصلہِ عمل کی کمی اور توانائی کی کمی ہو سکتی ہے۔ ایک معنی میں، آپ محض معمول کے مطابق کام کر رہے ہیں اور بس گزارہ کرنے کے لیے کافی کر رہے ہیں — چاہے کام پر ہوں یا گھر میں۔ یہ ممکنہ طور پر آپ کی ناامیدی کے احساس سے متعلق ہے۔

آپ محسوس کر سکتے ہیں کہ آپ پہلے سے زیادہ چڑچڑے ہو گئے ہیں۔ چھوٹی چھوٹی باتیں آپ کو پریشان یا چڑچڑا کر دیتی ہیں، اور آپ خود کو اس غصّے کے منہ تھامتے ہوئے پاتے ہیں۔

یہ سمجھنا ضروری ہے کہ آپ اس راہ پر کئی وجوہات کی بنا پر جا رہے ہیں۔ سب سے پہلے، جب آپ برن آؤٹ میں ہوتے ہیں تو صرف آپ ہی نہیں جو نقصان اٹھاتے ہیں۔ آپ کا خاندان آپ کے ‘‘بدمزگی’’ کا سامنا کرتا ہے۔ نیز، جتنا آپ بات کو نظر انداز کرتے رہیں گے، اتنا ہی مشکل ہوگا کہ دوبارہ توازن والے مقام تک پہنچا جائے۔

ایک طبیب کے طور پر، میں اکثر لوگوں کو دیکھتا ہوں جن کے پاس ‘‘وقت نہیں تھا’’ کسی چیز کا علاج کروانے کے لیے جب تک کہ وہ اسے نظر انداز نہ کر سکیں۔ اس نقطۂ نظر پر پہنچنے کے بعد، بڑے طریقۂ کار کی ضرورت ہوگی کہ حالات درست ہوں۔ اگر وہ پہلی علامت کے ساتھ آتے تو آسانی سے درست ہو سکتا تھا۔

ایک ترجیحی فہرست بنائیں

ہماری زندگی میں ہر چیز کی ایک ترجیحی سطح ہوتی ہے۔ جو لوگ ترجیحات مرتب نہیں کرتے وہ ہر چیز ایک ساتھ کرنے کی کوشش میں منتشر محسوس کرتے ہیں۔ یہ تباہی کی ترکیب ہے۔ میرے خیال میں، ہمارے کاموں کو چار بالٹیوں میں تقسیم کرنا سمجھ میں آتا ہے:

  1. وہ چیزیں جو نسبتاً جلدی کی جانی چاہئیں
  2. وہ چیزیں جو کرنی چاہئیں مگر تھوڑی دیر انتظار کر سکتیں
  3. وہ چیزیں جو ہم کرنا پسند کریں گے، مگر ضروری نہیں ہیں
  4. وہ چیزیں جنہیں ہمیں چھوڑ دینا چاہیے۔

یہاں یہ ذکر کرنا اچھا ہے کہ صرف اس لیے کہ کوئی چیز کرنی ضروری ہے اس کا مطلب یہ نہیں کہ آپ کو ہی کرنا ہے۔ کبھی کبھی آپ کے گھر یا کام کی جگہ پر کوئی اور آپ کی ٹو ڈو لسٹ کے کسی کام میں مدد کر سکتا ہے۔

ایک بار جب ہم نے اپنی ترجیحی فہرست بنالی، تو ہمیں اس کے بارے میں کچھ کرنا ہوگا۔ اگر آپ صرف ہر چیز کو ترجیح دیں اور پھر بھی سب کچھ کرنے کی کوشش کریں گے تو یہ آپ کی صورتِ حال کو بالکل بھی بہتر نہیں کرے گا۔

اس مشق کا مقصد یہ معلوم کرنا ہے کہ آپ اپنے شیڈول سے کون سی چیزیں نکال سکتے ہیں، تاکہ آپ کے پاس سانس لینے کی مزید جگہ ہو۔

اولیٰ باتیں پہلے رکھیں

جب ہم مغلوب ہوتے ہیں تو ایک چیز جو ہوتی ہے وہ ہے خود کی دیکھ بھال کو ترک کر دینا۔ ہم راستے میں غیر صحت مند غذا لے لیتے ہیں، دعا اور روحانی مطالعے میں وقت گزارنا چھوڑ دیتے ہیں، اور ورزش کرنا بند کر دیتے ہیں۔

یہ چیزیں کرنے میں وقت لگتا ہے، اور جب ہم اپنی توانائی کی حدوں پر زندگی گزار رہے ہوتے ہیں تو ہمیں یہی لگتا ہے کہ ہمارے پاس وقت نہیں ہے۔ خود کی دیکھ بھال انتہائی اہم ہے مگر اکثر اسے صفر ترجیح دی جاتی ہے اور کثرت سے دن کی سرگرمیوں میں شامل نہیں ہوتی۔

جیسے ہی ہم اپنی روحانی غذا کو بھرنا شروع کریں، ہمیں یہ بھی یقینی بنانا چاہیے کہ ہم اپنی جسمانی صحت کا خیال رکھیں۔

الگ ہونے کے لیے وقت نکالیں

ہجوم کو کھانا کھلانے کے بعد، مرقس 6:46 ہمیں بتاتا ہے کہ عیسی نے “اور جب اس نے انہیں رخصت کر دیا، تو وہ ایک پہاڑ کی طرف گیا تاکہ دعا کرے۔” حتی کہ عیسی کو بھی ایسے اوقات درکار تھے جب وہ خلوت میں ہوں بغیر کسی خلفشار کے۔

اس آیت کے دعا کے پہلو پر توجہ دینا آسان ہے، اور یہ اہم ہے، مگر آئیں اس تجربے کے تنہائی والے پہلو پر توجہ دیں۔ عیسی نے اس وقت اپنے قریب ترین پیروکاروں کو پیچھے بھی چھوڑ دیا تھا جب وہ خدا کا چہرہ تلاش کر رہے تھے۔

ایسے اوقات ہوتے ہیں جب ہمیں انسانی تعاملات کے دباؤ سے فرار حاصل کر کے ایک پرامن جگہ تلاش کرنے کی ضرورت ہوتی ہے جہاں ہم اکیلے رہ سکیں۔

ٹیکنالوجی کو نیچے رکھیں

آرام کے وقت کو واقعی آرام دہ بنانے کا ایک حصہ خلفشار کے ذرائع ختم کرنا ہے۔ فون اور الیکٹرانک ٹیبلیٹس بالکل وہی چیزیں ہیں جو ہمارے ذہنوں کو وہ سکون (شالوم) حاصل کرنے سے روک سکتی ہیں جو ہم چاہتے اور ضرورت رکھتے ہیں۔

ڈیجیٹل برن آؤٹ ایک نیا اصطلاح ہے جو ایسے لوگوں کی وضاحت کے لیے استعمال ہو رہا ہے جو گھنٹوں روزانہ سکرینوں کو گھورتے رہنے سے بیزار اور تھکے ہوئے محسوس کرتے ہیں۔ بہت سے کارکن روزانہ سات یا آٹھ گھنٹے کمپیوٹر سکرینز دیکھتے ہیں اور پھر کام کے بعد بھی اور سکرین ٹائم لے لیتے ہیں۔

دلچسپ بات یہ ہے کہ سب سے زیادہ پیداواری کارکن اکثر وہ لوگ ہوتے ہیں جو پرانے انداز کی چیزیں استعمال کرتے ہیں جیسے کاغذی کیلنڈر اور میٹنگز میں فون باہر نہیں رکھتے۔ جتنے شاندار فون ہیں، وہ بھی ہمارے لیے بہت زیادہ خلفشار کا باعث بنتے ہیں۔

اکثر ہمارے پاس جو دوری کا وقت ہوتا ہے وہ حقیقت میں آرام دہ نہیں ہوتا۔ وجہ یہ ہے کہ ہم مسلسل ٹیکسٹ اور ای میلز وصول کرتے رہتے ہیں اور سوشل میڈیا تک رسائی رکھتے ہیں۔ اگر آپ وہ شخص نہیں جو اپنا فون رکھ کر نظرانداز کر سکے (اس کے لیے بہت زیادہ قوتِ ارادی چاہیے)، تو پھر فون کو دوسرے کمرے میں چھوڑ دیں اور فاصلہ قائم کریں۔ یہ دباؤ محسوس ہوگا، مگر ہم خود کو ریچارج کرنے پر توجہ مرکوز کر سکتے ہیں اگر ہم ایک اسکرین فری زون بنائیں۔

اپنے دن میں وقفے بنائیں

روزانہ ایک مخصوص مقدار میں کام ہوتا ہے جو کرنا ضروری ہے، اور یہ اکثر مقررہ 24 گھنٹوں کے لیے بہت زیادہ محسوس ہوتا ہے۔ یقیناً رُک کر کھینچنے یا پانچ منٹ کی سیر کرنے کا وقت نہیں ہوتا، یا کم از کم ہم خود سے یہی کہتے ہیں۔

حقیقت یہ ہے کہ اگر آپ چند گھنٹوں کے وقفے کے بعد ہر چند گھنٹے میں پانچ منٹ کا بریک لیتے ہیں اور غیر کام سے متعلق کوئی کام کرتے ہیں تو آپ تازہ دم ہو کر واپس آئیں گے اور دن کے مسائل سے نمٹنے کے لیے زیادہ تیار ہوں گے۔

اس وقت کے دوران کوئی صحت مند کام کریں۔ ایک مختصر چہل قدمی کریں یا ایک سیب کھائیں۔ چپس کا تھیلا کھا جانا یا چند کینڈی بارز کھانا مطلوبہ نتائج نہیں دے گا۔

مسئلہ اکثر ہماری اپنی توقعات کے ساتھ ہوتا ہے۔ برن آؤٹ میں جدوجہد کرنے والے لوگ اکثر انتہائی بلند ذاتی معیار رکھتے ہیں اور جب وہ اس معیار پر پورا نہیں اترتے تو مایوس ہو جاتے ہیں۔

آرام کے بارے میں ارادہ مند رہیں

عہد نامۂ عتیق کا ایک پیغام ہفتے کے آرام (Sabbath) کی اہمیت تھا۔ میں نے کئی لوگوں کو سنا ہے جو دلیل دیتے ہیں کہ نئے عہد نامے کے دور میں ہمیں اب شبات کی مشق کرنے کی ضرورت نہیں۔ کیا پولُس نے نہیں کہا کہ ایک دن دوسرے کے برابر ہے؟ کیا عیسیٰ نے اپنے شاگردوں کا دفاع نہیں کیا جب وہ شبات کو اناج توڑ رہے تھے؟

چاہے آپ شبات رکھنے کی اہمیت کے بارے میں جو کچھ بھی مانتے ہوں، پھر بھی یہ ضروری ہے کہ ہم آرام کے لیے وقت نکالیں۔ یہی حقیقی پیغام ہے جو عیسی نے اُس وقت پہنچایا جب انہوں نے کہا کہ “شبات انسان کے لیے بنایا گیا تھا، انسان شبات کے لیے نہیں” (مرقس 2:27)۔

آرام صرف صبح دس بجے تک سونا اور پھر کچھ نہ کرنا نہیں ہے۔ آرام وہ فعال فیصلے کرنا ہے جو ہماری کمی شدہ بیٹریاں دوبارہ چارج کرنے میں مدد کریں۔ کسی دوست کے ساتھ ناشتے کے لیے باہر جائیں، ایک پہاڑی سیر پر جائیں، یا کوئی اچھی کتاب لے کر کہیں جائیں جہاں سیل سروس نہ ہو اور اُن چیزوں پر توجہ مرکوز کریں جو آپ کو نِکال رہی ہیں۔

عیسیٰ انسان کی آرام کی ضرورت کو سمجھتے تھے، اسی لیے انہوں نے اپنے شاگردوں سے کہا “خود تم ایک طرف چلو اور تھوڑا آرام کرو” (مرقس 6:31)۔ یہ آرام کا وقت انہیں اپنی اگلی وزارت کے لیے توانائی دے گا۔

افسانوں میں نہ آ جائیں

لوگ اپنے آپ کو طرح طرح کی جھوٹ بولتے ہیں جو انہیں بہت زیادہ زور لگانے پر مائل کر دیتے ہیں۔ میں ان میں سے چند ایک کا ذکر کروں گا اور ہر ایک کے بارے میں کچھ خیالات دوں گا۔

“میں ہی وہ واحد ہوں جو یہ کام کر سکتا ہوں۔” یہ سچ محسوس ہوتا ہے۔ ہمارے گھر یا کام کی جگہ کے دوسرے لوگ ویسے مدد نہیں کر رہے جیسا ہم چاہیں گے۔ کبھی کبھی، کسی کو کام سکھانے میں وقت گزارنے کے بجائے خود کرنا آسان محسوس ہوتا ہے۔ ہمیں یاد رکھنا چاہیے کہ اگر ہم مر گئے تو ہمارے آس پاس کے لوگ کام کرنے کا طریقہ سیکھ لیں گے۔ ہم آج ہی انہیں کچھ کام سونپ سکتے ہیں۔

“اگر میں آج یہ کام ختم کر دوں تو کل آسان ہوگا۔” مجھے بری خبر سناتے ہوئے دکھ ہوتا ہے، مگر ہر دن میں 24 گھنٹے ہوتے ہیں، اور کسی طرح وہ ہمیشہ بھر جاتے ہیں۔ میں نے اس خیال کو چھوڑ دیا ہے کہ میری زندگی میں جلد ہی کوئی ایسا وقت آئے گا جس میں شیڈول خالی ہو گا۔ اگر آرام آتا ہے تو وہ اس لیے آئے گا کہ میں نے اپنی شیڈول صاف کرنے کی کوشش کی ہے، نہ کہ اس لیے کہ کسی حادثاتی واقعے کی وجہ سے کسی ایک دن میرے پاس ایک بھی کام نہ ہو۔

“خدا مجھے کبھی اتنا زیادہ نہیں دے گا کہ میں برداشت نہ کر سکوں۔” خدا نے بہت سی باتوں کا وعدہ کیا ہے۔ اس نے وعدہ کیا ہے کہ جب کسی آزمائش میں ہم ہوں گے تو وہ ہمیں ایک راستہ فرار دینے کا موقع دے گا (پہلا کرنتھیوں 10:13). اس نے یہ بھی وعدہ کیا ہے کہ وہ ہمیں کبھی نہیں چھوڑے گا اور نہ ہی ترک کرے گا (عبرانیوں 13:5). میں صحیفے میں کہیں یہ نہیں پڑھتا کہ خدا ہمیں اپنی زندگیوں کو زیادہ بھرنے سے روکے گا۔ اس نے محض وعدہ کیا ہے کہ وہ ہمیں ایک متبادل راستہ دکھائے گا اور ہمارے راستے میں ہمارے ساتھ چلے گا۔

اکثر ہمارا بھاری بوجھ اس لیے ہوتا ہے کہ دوسرے لوگ، یا یہاں تک کہ ہم خود، اپنی ٹو ڈو لسٹ میں بہت سی چیزیں شامل کر دیتے ہیں۔ فرض کریں میں نے اپنے شیڈول میں بہت سے مریض رکھ لیے اور میں تھکا ہوا محسوس کر رہا ہوں۔ اس صورت میں یہ وقت ہے کہ میں اس کی ذمہ داری قبول کروں جو میں نے کی ہے، بجائے اس کے کہ میں کسی افسانوی وعدے کا سہارا لوں کہ خدا مجھے خود بخود حد سے زیادہ بوجھ اٹھانے سے بچا لے گا۔

“یہ سب اچھے کام ہیں جو میں کر رہا ہوں۔” ڈاکٹروں کو یہ مسئلہ بہت پیش آتا ہے۔ ہم ایک اور مریض کو ٹائٹ شیڈول میں دابنا چاہتے ہیں اور تھوڑا دیر تک رہ کر ایک اور پیغام کا جواب دینا چاہتے ہیں کیونکہ ہمیں ذمہ دار محسوس ہوتا ہے۔ ہم اس خیال کو گوارا نہیں کرتے کہ شاید کسی کو ایمرجنسی ڈیپارٹمنٹ جانا پڑے کیونکہ ہم نے وقت پر ان کی مدد نہ کی۔

صرف اس لیے کہ آپ کے شیڈول کی چیزیں “اچھے کام” ہیں جو دوسروں کے فائدے اور بادشاہی کی تعمیر کرتی ہیں، اس کا مطلب یہ نہیں کہ آپ کو کسی ایک جگہ سے پیچھے ہٹنے کی ضرورت نہیں۔ اگر آپ جذباتی طور پر خالی محسوس کر رہے ہیں تو شاید کسی ایک یا دو چیزوں کو اپنی فہرست سے نکالنے کا وقت آ گیا ہے۔

نتیجہ

اور بھی چیزیں ہیں جن کا ذکر کیا جا سکتا تھا۔ کسی سے مدد لینا، صحیفے پر غور و فکر کرنا، اور یہاں تک کہ ایک تعطیل پر جانا ایسی چیزیں ہیں جو مدد کر سکتی ہیں۔

جب میں ماضی کے کچھ مشہور مبلغین کے بارے میں پڑھتا ہوں تو میں ان کی زندگیوں میں ایک رولر کوسٹر دیکھتا ہوں۔ وہ خود کو حدِ اعلٰی تک دھکیلتے، بہت سی منصوبوں میں ملوث ہو جاتے، اور پھر جذباتی طور پر ٹوٹ پڑتے۔ وہ کچھ وقت کے لیے آرام کرتے اور ایک یا دو ماہ بعد پھر اسی سرگرمی میں جھپٹ پڑتے۔ یہ سائیکل ان کی پوری وزارت کے دوران جاری رہا۔

عیسیٰ ہمیں بتاتے ہیں کہ اُس کا یُوق ہلکا ہے اور اُس کا بوجھ نرم ہے (متی 11:28-30). اگر ہم فرسودگی کے مقام پر ہیں تو ہمیں غور کرنا چاہیے کہ کیا ہمارے پاس عیسیٰ کا یُوق ہے یا ہم نے خود अपना बनाया ہوا بوجھ اٹھا رکھا ہے۔

عیسیٰ ہماری حدوں کو جانتے ہیں۔ وہ چاہتے ہیں کہ ہم توازن کے ساتھ زندگی گزاریں، اس طرح کہ ہمارے پاس نہ صرف آج کی طاقت ہو بلکہ کل، اگلے ہفتے، اور اگلے سال تک — جب تک وہ دوبارہ نہ آئیں۔

The message was brief. “Dr. Waldron, would you call Mrs. Jones back about her labs?”

I was puzzled. I didn’t remember ordering any labs for Mrs. Jones. As far as I could remember, she was seeing a specialist and just had surgery for colon cancer. Maybe they had ordered the labs. But if so, they certainly should have followed up on them.

I opened the chart and looked in the lab section. Quickly my eye went to my patient’s kidney function and stopped. Her kidney function had declined a huge amount in the last week.

I called her and then her kidney specialist. Over the next half hour, her situation came into view. Because of her colon surgery, she was losing a lot of fluid, enough that she couldn’t keep up. This, in turn, was making her kidney function a lot worse, along with dropping her potassium level.

To take care of it, she would need IV fluids – once or twice a week – to keep up with the fluids she was losing. Without that, her kidneys would shut down completely.

In a sense, Mrs. Jones was dealing with kidney burnout—a situation where they were putting out more than they were taking in and suffering as a result.

As I was thinking about this, my mind went to the Dead Sea. The Dead Sea is “Dead” because it has such a high level of minerals and salts that very few, other than a few microorganisms, can survive.

The reason for this is that the Dead Sea has no outlet. The Jordan River drains into it, carrying fresh water, and then sits in a basin. Some of the water evaporates, and what remains are the salts and minerals in the water.

Over the thousands of years since the fall of Sodom and Gomorrah, this inland body of water has become one of the saltiest places on earth. It is a body of water that is neither useful for irrigation nor a place where plants and animals can thrive.

Neither situation is healthy, yet this is exactly how most people live their lives, typically gravitating towards one pole or the other. Either they fill their schedule to the maximum, leaving no time for quiet reflection, or they resist any efforts to get them to invest their time and talents and avoid these sorts of activities.

I want to spend a little time thinking about burnout. What causes it, and how we can avoid it?

Everyone has Limits

I Samuel 30 tells the story of David returning to Ziklag. Upon his arrival, he discovered, to his dismay, that the Amalekites had invaded Philistine territory, burned the town, and taken captive all the people who were present.

David and his men had been gone three days and were already tired from their journey to and from Aphek, where King Agag had mustered his forces. Despite this and their anguish at the loss of their family members and material possessions, David consulted God and decided to pursue to the Amalekites out into the desert.

They had only gone as far as the Brook Besor when a third of his men gave up. Scripture tells us they were “too faint” to cross the brook. They were physically and mentally exhausted. Even if they had been able to hold things together for another day, they would be useless in battle.

So it was that David left them behind and continued to pursue the Amalekites, eventually defeating them with the four hundred men who were able to persevere. Here, we come to the interesting part. The men who had won the victory looked down on the men who had been faint. They said those faint-hearted men could have their families back, but all the spoil would be reserved for those who had won the victory.

In response, David said, “Ye shall not do so, my brethren, with that which the Lord hath given us, who hath preserved us, and delivered the company that came against us into our hand. For who will hearken unto you in this matter? but as his part is that goeth down to the battle, so shall his part be that tarrieth by the stuff: they shall part alike.” (I Samuel 30:23,24)

David did not wish to penalize those who had tried but did not have the strength to make it through to the final battle.

Perhaps this speaks of the grace we ought to extend to others who don’t have the strength or energy to continue for a season. Maybe it lets us know that we should extend that same grace to ourselves.

What is Burnout?

There are different definitions for burnout, but it all comes down to a state of physical, mental, or emotional exhaustion related to too much stress over an extended period of time. We tend to think of this stress as work-related. There are too many projects going on at once, not enough help, or an employer who has high expectations.

Stress is stress, and it all adds up. Even if work isn’t stressful, if you have a newborn baby at home, a family member with dementia, or many church responsibilities, you can still reach the place where you have little left to give.

It is as though you are in a vehicle traveling 90 mph, and you push the accelerator a little harder, and nothing happens. In response, you push the gas pedal even harder, and a screeching noise comes from the engine. Suddenly, the dashboard lights up with funny lights, and the car starts to slow down.

The question is, how can we avoid burnout and what should we do if we realize that we are heading towards it?

Understanding Burnout

Burnout leads to both physical and emotional depletion. The problem with burnout is that even if a particular stressor causes it – say, a situation at work or a family health problem – it will affect numerous other relationships.

People dealing with burnout often exhibit symptoms consistent with depression and anxiety. They may become withdrawn, lack motivation to be involved with church and family activities, or get angry quicker than people who are not dealing with burnout.

There is even a suggestion that burnout can lead to the weakening of our immune systems. This could lead to more colds and viral infections.

Identify Early Signs

We need to know ourselves. There are signs that other people can see in our lives and how we relate to others that we don’t necessarily identify as a problem.

People who are on the edge of burnout feel hopeless. They may hide it from their coworkers, but often, their family members realize that something is wrong. You used to have a sunny disposition, and now you are discouraged, not only about the present but also the future.

You might lack motivation and have low energy levels. In a sense, you are going through the motions and just doing enough to get by – both at work and in your home. This is likely related to your feelings of hopelessness.

You may find that you are more irritable than you used to be. Little things bother or aggravate you, and you find yourself smothering angry retorts.

It is important to realize that you are heading down this road for several reasons. First, you are not the only one who suffers when you are burned out. Your family must deal with you and your “grumpiness.” Also, the longer you go without taking care of things, the harder it is to get back to a place of balance.

As a physician, I see people all the time who “didn’t have time” to get something taken care of until they could no longer ignore it. At this point, it will take a major procedure to set things right. It would have been easier to correct if they came in with the first symptom.

Make a Priority List

Everything in our life has a priority level. People who do not prioritize end up feeling scattered as they try to do everything at once. This is a recipe for disaster. To me, it makes sense to divide our tasks into four buckets:

  1. Things that need to be done relatively quickly
  2. Things that need to be done but can wait a bit
  3. Things that we’d like to do, but don’t need to
  4. Things that we should let go of.

Here might be a good place to mention that just because something needs to be done does not mean you need to do it. Sometimes, someone in your home or workplace could help with one of the tasks on your to-do list.

Once we have made our priority list, we need to do something about it. If you simply assign a priority to everything in your life but continue to try to do everything, it won’t help your situation at all.

The point of this exercise is to figure out what things you can eliminate from your schedule, so you have more space to breathe.

Make First Things First

One of the things that happens when we are overwhelmed is that we stop doing self-care. We grab unhealthy food on the go, stop spending time in prayer and devotions, and quit exercising.

Doing these things takes time, and that is exactly what we think we don’t have when we are living on the margins of our energy. Self-care is extremely important but often gets assigned a priority of zero and is seldom included in a day’s activity.

As we begin to replenish our spiritual nourishment, we must also make sure we take care of our physical health.

Take Time Apart

After feeding the multitudes, Mark 6:46 tells of Jesus, “And when he had sent them away, he departed into a mountain to pray.” Even Jesus had times when He needed to be alone without distractions.

It is easy to focus on the prayer aspect of this passage, and that is important, but let's focus on the solitary aspect of this experience. Jesus even left His closest followers behind during this time of seeking God’s face.

There are times when we need to escape from the pressure of human interactions and find a peaceful place where we can be alone.

Put Down Technology

Part of making rest time truly restful is to eliminate sources of distraction. Phones and electronic tablets are exactly the types of things that can keep our minds from achieving the peace (shalom) that we both desire and need.

Digital burnout is a new term that is being used to describe people who feel apathetic and exhausted from spending hours each day staring at screens. Many workers spend seven or eight hours a day looking at computer screens and then get even more screen time after work.

The funny thing is that the most productive workers are often people who use old-fashioned things like paper calendars and leave phones out of meetings. As wonderful as phones are, they are also immensely distracting for most of us.

So often, we have time away that is simply not restful. The reason is that we continue to receive texts and emails and can still access social media. If you are not someone who can put his phone away and ignore it (it takes a lot of willpower to do this), then leave your phone in another room and create some distance. This will seem stressful, but we can focus on recharging ourselves by creating a screen-free zone.

Build Breaks into Your Day

There is a certain amount of work that must be done each day, and it often feels like too much for the allotted 24 hours. There is certainly no time to stop, stretch, and take a five-minute walk, or at least that's what we tell ourselves.

In reality, if you take a five-minute break every few hours to do something non-work related, you will come back refreshed and more ready to deal with the problems of the day.

Do something healthy during this time. Take a short walk or eat an apple. Chowing down a bag of potato chips or eating a couple candy bars is not likely to produce the desired results.

The problem is often with our own expectations. People who struggle with burnout often have extremely high personal standards and get frustrated when they not measure up to that standard.

Be Intentional about Rest

One of the messages of the Old Testament was the importance of the Sabbath. I have heard many people argue that in the New Testament period, we no longer need to practice the Sabbath. Didn’t Paul say that one day was like the other? Didn’t Jesus defend His disciples for picking grain on the Sabbath?

Regardless of what you believe about the importance of keeping the Sabbath, it is still important that we take time to rest. This is the real message that Jesus was conveying when He said that the “Sabbath was created for man, not man for the Sabbath” (Mark 2:27).

Rest is not simply sleeping till 10 am and then doing nothing. Rest is actively making decisions that will help us recharge our depleted batteries. Go out for breakfast with a friend, take a hike, or take a good book and go somewhere without cell service and focus on something other than situations that are depleting you.

Jesus understood the human need for rest, this is why He told His disciples “Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while” (Mark 6:31). This time of rest would give them energy for their next time of ministry.

Don’t Buy into Myths

People tell themselves all sorts of lies that can lead to pushing themselves too hard. I’ll list a few of them and some thoughts about each one.

“I’m the only one who can do this task.” This feels true. The other people in our home or workplace are not helping us the way we wish that they would. Sometimes, it simply feels easier to do the task ourselves rather than spend time teaching someone else how to do it. We need to remember that if we died, the people around us would figure out how to get things done. We can assign them some of the tasks today before we die.

“If I just get this job done today, tomorrow will be easier.” I hate to be the bearer of bad news, but each day has 24 hours, and somehow, they always get filled up. I have given up the idea that there is a time in my life coming up soon that will have nothing on the schedule. If a rest comes, it will come because I have made an effort to clear my schedule, not because by some random occurrence, one day, I happen to not have a single task in it.

“God will never give me more than I can handle.” God has promised many things. He has promised that when there is a temptation, He will give us an opportunity to escape it (I Corinthians 10:13). He has also promised that He will never leave us or forsake us (Hebrews 13:5). I do not read anywhere in Scripture that God will keep us from overfilling our lives. He has simply promised that He will give us opportunity to take a different path and will walk beside us on our way.

So often the heavy load we carry is because other people, or even we, ourselves, have put too many things on our task list. Suppose I choose to put too many patients on my schedule and I am feeling exhausted. In that case, it is time for me to take responsibility for what I have done, rather than claiming a mythical promise that God will keep me from overwhelming myself.

“These are all good things that I am doing.” Doctors face this a lot. We want to squeeze one more patient into the schedule and stay just a little later to answer another message because we feel responsible. We hate to think that someone might need to go to the Emergency Department because we did not take care of them when they needed help.

Just because the things in your schedule are “good things” that benefit other people and are building the kingdom, does not mean that you don’t need to cut back in one area or another. If you are feeling emotionally depleted, it is probably time to remove a few items from your to-do list.

Conclusion

There are other things that could be mentioned. Getting support from someone else, meditating on Scripture, and even taking a vacation are all things that can help.

When I read about some of the famous preachers of the past, I see in some of their lives a roller coaster. They pushed themselves to the max, got involved in large numbers of projects, and then had an emotional breakdown. They would take some time off and, a month or two later, launch back into the same activities. This cycle continued for their whole ministry.

Jesus tells us that His yoke is easy, and His burden is light (Matt, 11:28-30). If we are at the point of exhaustion, we need to consider whether we have Jesus’ yoke or if we are laboring under the burden of our own creation.

Jesus knows our limitations. He wants us to have balance, living in such a way that we not only have strength for today but also for tomorrow, next week, and next year – till He comes again.

Pelo que eu me lembrava, ela estava sendo atendida por um especialista e acabara de fazer uma cirurgia por câncer de cólon. Talvez eles tivessem solicitado os exames. Mas, se foi esse o caso, certamente deveriam ter feito o acompanhamento.

Abri o prontuário e olhei a seção de exames. Rapidamente meu olhar foi para a função renal da minha paciente e parou. A função renal dela havia caído enormemente na última semana.

Liguei para ela e depois para o nefrologista. Ao longo da meia hora seguinte, a situação dela ficou clara. Por causa da cirurgia de cólon, ela estava perdendo muito líquido, o suficiente para que não conseguisse repor. Isso, por sua vez, estava piorando muito a função renal, além de baixar o nível de potássio.

Para cuidar disso, ela precisaria de fluidos intravenosos – uma ou duas vezes por semana – para repor os líquidos que estava perdendo. Sem isso, os rins dela parariam completamente.

De certa forma, a Sra. Jones estava lidando com um esgotamento renal—uma situação em que eles estão perdendo mais do que recebem e sofrem como resultado.

Enquanto pensava nisso, minha mente foi para o Mar Morto. O Mar Morto é “morto” porque tem um nível tão alto de minerais e sais que muito poucos, além de alguns microrganismos, conseguem sobreviver ali.

O motivo é que o Mar Morto não tem saída. O rio Jordão deságua nele, trazendo água doce, que então permanece numa bacia. Parte da água evapora, e o que fica são os sais e minerais presentes na água.

Ao longo dos milhares de anos desde a queda de Sodoma e Gomorra, esse corpo de água interior tornou-se um dos lugares mais salgados da terra. É um corpo de água que não é útil para irrigação nem um lugar onde plantas e animais possam prosperar.

Nenhuma das situações é saudável, e ainda assim é exatamente assim que a maioria das pessoas vive suas vidas, tipicamente gravitando para um polo ou outro. Ou elas enchem sua agenda ao máximo, sem deixar tempo para reflexão tranquila, ou resistem a quaisquer esforços para que invistam seu tempo e talentos, evitando esse tipo de atividade.

Quero dedicar um pouco de tempo a pensar sobre o esgotamento. O que o causa e como podemos evitá‑lo?

Todos têm Limites

1 Samuel 30 conta a história de Davi retornando a Ziclague. Ao chegar, descobriu, para seu desespero, que os amalequitas haviam invadido o território filisteu, queimado a cidade e feito prisioneiras todas as pessoas que estavam presentes.

Davi e seus homens tinham estado fora por três dias e já estavam cansados da jornada de ida e volta a Afeque, onde o rei Agague havia reunido suas forças. Apesar disso e da angústia pela perda de parentes e bens materiais, Davi consultou a Deus e decidiu perseguir os amalequitas pelo deserto.

Eles só haviam chegado até o ribeiro de Besor quando um terço dos seus homens desistiu. A Escritura nos diz que estavam “muito cansados” para atravessar o ribeiro. Estavam esgotados física e mentalmente. Mesmo que tivessem conseguido manter a compostura por mais um dia, seriam inúteis em batalha.

Assim Davi os deixou para trás e continuou a perseguir os amalequitas, eventualmente derrotando‑os com os quatrocentos homens que conseguiram perseverar. Aqui chegamos à parte interessante. Os homens que conquistaram a vitória desprezaram os que haviam se cansado. Disseram que esses homens abatidos poderiam ficar com suas famílias, mas todo o despojo seria reservado para os que haviam vencido a batalha.

Em resposta, Davi disse: “Não fareis assim, irmãos meus, com o que o Senhor nos deu, que nos tem guardado e entregado na nossa mão a companhia que subiu contra nós. Porque quem vos ouvirá neste negócio? porém, como é a parte daquele que vai à peleja, assim será a parte daquele que fica junto às coisas: repartirão igualmente.” (I Samuel 30:23,24)

Davi não quis penalizar aqueles que tentaram, mas não tiveram forças para chegar até a batalha final.

Talvez isso fale da graça que devemos estender a outros que não têm força ou energia para continuar por uma temporada. Talvez nos diga que devemos estender essa mesma graça a nós mesmos.

O que é Esgotamento?

Existem diferentes definições para esgotamento, mas tudo se resume a um estado de exaustão física, mental ou emocional relacionado a muito estresse por um período prolongado. Tendemos a pensar nesse estresse como relacionado ao trabalho. Há muitos projetos acontecendo ao mesmo tempo, ajuda insuficiente, ou um empregador com expectativas altas.

Estresse é estresse, e tudo se acumula. Mesmo que o trabalho não seja estressante, se você tem um bebê recém‑nascido em casa, um membro da família com demência ou muitas responsabilidades na igreja, ainda pode chegar ao ponto em que tem pouco a oferecer.

É como se você estivesse em um veículo a 140 km/h, apertasse um pouco mais o acelerador e nada acontecesse. Em resposta, você pisa ainda mais no acelerador, e um ruído estridente vem do motor. De repente, o painel acende com luzes estranhas, e o carro começa a perder velocidade.

A pergunta é: como podemos evitar o esgotamento e o que devemos fazer se percebermos que estamos caminhando na direção dele?

Compreendendo o Esgotamento

O esgotamento leva ao esvaziamento tanto físico quanto emocional. O problema do esgotamento é que, mesmo que um estressor particular o cause – por exemplo, uma situação no trabalho ou um problema de saúde na família – ele afetará inúmeros outros relacionamentos.

Pessoas que lidam com esgotamento frequentemente exibem sintomas compatíveis com depressão e ansiedade. Podem se tornar reservadas, perder motivação para se envolver em atividades da igreja e da família, ou se irritarem mais rapidamente do que pessoas que não estão passando por esgotamento.

Há até a sugestão de que o esgotamento pode levar ao enfraquecimento do nosso sistema imunológico. Isso poderia resultar em mais gripes e infecções virais.

Identifique os Sinais Precoce

Precisamos nos conhecer. Existem sinais que outras pessoas conseguem ver em nossas vidas e em como nos relacionamos com os outros que nós nem sempre identificamos como um problema.

Pessoas que estão à beira do esgotamento sentem‑se sem esperança. Podem esconder isso dos colegas, mas frequentemente os familiares percebem que algo está errado. Você costumava ter um temperamento ensolarado, e agora está desencorajado, não apenas em relação ao presente, mas também ao futuro.

Você pode faltar motivação e ter níveis baixos de energia. Em certo sentido, você faz as coisas mecanicamente e apenas o suficiente para sobreviver – tanto no trabalho quanto em casa. Isso provavelmente está relacionado aos seus sentimentos de desesperança.

Pode descobrir que está mais irritável do que costumava ser. Coisas pequenas incomodam ou irritam você, e se pega contendo respostas de raiva.

É importante perceber que você está seguindo por esse caminho por várias razões. Primeiro, você não é o único que sofre quando está esgotado. Sua família tem de lidar com você e com sua “rabugice”. Além disso, quanto mais tempo você demora para cuidar das coisas, mais difícil é voltar a um ponto de equilíbrio.

Como médico, vejo pessoas o tempo todo que “não tiveram tempo” de tratar algo até que não puderam mais ignorar. Nesse ponto, será necessário um procedimento maior para corrigir a situação. Teria sido mais fácil resolver se tivessem vindo com o primeiro sintoma.

Faça uma Lista de Prioridades

Tudo em nossa vida tem um nível de prioridade. Pessoas que não priorizam acabam sentindo‑se dispersas ao tentar fazer tudo ao mesmo tempo. Isso é uma receita para o desastre. Para mim, faz sentido dividir nossas tarefas em quatro baldes:

  1. Coisas que precisam ser feitas relativamente rápido
  2. Coisas que precisam ser feitas, mas podem esperar um pouco
  3. Coisas que gostaríamos de fazer, mas não são necessárias
  4. Coisas das quais deveríamos nos desligar.

Talvez seja um bom momento para mencionar que só porque algo precisa ser feito não significa que você precise fazê‑lo. Às vezes, alguém em sua casa ou local de trabalho pode ajudar com uma das tarefas da sua lista.

Uma vez que tenhamos feito nossa lista de prioridades, precisamos agir. Se você simplesmente atribuir prioridade a tudo na sua vida, mas continuar tentando fazer tudo, isso não ajudará em nada.

O objetivo deste exercício é descobrir o que pode ser eliminado da sua agenda, para que você tenha mais espaço para respirar.

Ponha as Primeiras Coisas em Primeiro Lugar

Uma das coisas que acontece quando estamos sobrecarregados é que paramos de cuidar de nós mesmos. Pegamos comida não saudável para comer rápido, deixamos de dedicar tempo à oração e devoções e paramos de nos exercitar.

Fazer essas coisas leva tempo, e é exatamente isso que pensamos não ter quando vivemos à margem da nossa energia. O autocuidado é extremamente importante, mas frequentemente recebe prioridade zero e raramente é incluído nas atividades do dia.

À medida que começamos a reabastecer nosso alimento espiritual, devemos também garantir que cuidamos da nossa saúde física.

Tire um Tempo a Sós

Depois de alimentar as multidões, Marcos 6:46 conta sobre Jesus: “E, tendo despedido a multidão, foi para o monte, a fim de orar.” Mesmo Jesus tinha momentos em que precisava ficar sozinho, sem distrações.

É fácil focar no aspecto da oração dessa passagem, e isso é importante, mas concentremo‑nos no aspecto solitário dessa experiência. Jesus até deixou seus seguidores mais próximos durante esse tempo de busca pela face de Deus.

Há momentos em que precisamos escapar da pressão das interações humanas e encontrar um lugar tranquilo onde possamos ficar a sós.

Desligue a Tecnologia

Parte de fazer com que o tempo de descanso seja realmente repousante é eliminar fontes de distração. Telefones e tablets eletrônicos são exatamente o tipo de coisa que pode impedir nossa mente de alcançar a paz (shalom) que desejamos e precisamos.

“Esgotamento digital” é um termo novo que vem sendo usado para descrever pessoas que se sentem apáticas e exaustas por passar horas por dia olhando para telas. Muitos trabalhadores passam sete ou oito horas por dia olhando para telas de computador e então têm ainda mais tempo de tela depois do trabalho.

O curioso é que os trabalhadores mais produtivos costumam ser pessoas que usam coisas à moda antiga, como calendários de papel, e deixam os telefones fora das reuniões. Por mais maravilhosos que sejam os telefones, também são imensamente distrativos para a maioria de nós.

Tantas vezes temos tempo livre que simplesmente não é repousante. A razão é que continuamos a receber mensagens de texto e e‑mails e ainda acessamos as redes sociais. Se você não é alguém que consegue guardar o telefone e ignorá‑lo (isso exige muita força de vontade), deixe o telefone em outro cômodo e crie alguma distância. Isso parecerá estressante, mas podemos nos concentrar em recarregar criando uma zona sem telas.

Inclua Pausas no Seu Dia

Há uma certa quantidade de trabalho que deve ser feita a cada dia, e muitas vezes parece demais para as 24 horas disponíveis. Certamente não há tempo para parar, alongar‑se e fazer uma caminhada de cinco minutos, ou pelo menos é o que dizemos a nós mesmos.

Na realidade, se você fizer uma pausa de cinco minutos a cada poucas horas para fazer algo não relacionado ao trabalho, voltará renovado e mais pronto para lidar com os problemas do dia.

Faça algo saudável durante esse tempo. Dê uma caminhada curta ou coma uma maçã. Devorar um saco de batata‑frita ou comer duas barras de chocolate provavelmente não produzirá os resultados desejados.

O problema costuma estar em nossas próprias expectativas. Pessoas que lutam com esgotamento frequentemente têm padrões pessoais extremamente altos e ficam frustradas quando não correspondem a esse padrão.

Seja Intencional quanto ao Descanso

Uma das mensagens do Antigo Testamento era a importância do sábado. Ouvi muitas pessoas argumentarem que, no período do Novo Testamento, já não precisamos praticar o sábado. Paulo não disse que um dia era como outro? Jesus não defendeu seus discípulos por colher espigas no sábado?

Independentemente do que você acredita sobre a importância de guardar o sábado, ainda é importante que tiremos tempo para descansar. Essa é a verdadeira mensagem que Jesus estava transmitindo quando disse que “o sábado foi feito por causa do homem, e não o homem por causa do sábado” (Marcos 2:27).

Descanso não é simplesmente dormir até as 10h e depois não fazer nada. Descanso é tomar decisões ativamente que nos ajudarão a recarregar nossas baterias esgotadas. Saia para tomar café da manhã com um amigo, faça uma trilha ou leve um bom livro a algum lugar sem sinal de celular e concentre‑se em algo diferente das situações que o estão esgotando.

Jesus compreendeu a necessidade humana de descanso; por isso lhes disse aos discípulos: “Vinde vós, à parte, para um lugar deserto, e repousai um pouco” (Marcos 6:31). Esse tempo de descanso lhes daria energia para o próximo tempo de ministério.

Não Acredite em Mitos

As pessoas contam a si mesmas todo tipo de mentira que pode levá‑las a se esforçar demais. Vou listar algumas delas e alguns pensamentos sobre cada uma.

“Sou a única pessoa que pode fazer esta tarefa.” Isso parece verdade. As outras pessoas em nossa casa ou local de trabalho não nos ajudam do jeito que gostaríamos. Às vezes, simplesmente parece mais fácil fazer a tarefa nós mesmos do que gastar tempo ensinando outra pessoa. Precisamos lembrar que, se morrêssemos, as pessoas ao nosso redor aprenderiam a fazer as coisas. Podemos atribuir algumas tarefas a elas hoje, antes de morrer.

“Se eu só terminar este trabalho hoje, amanhã será mais fácil.” Odeio ser portador de más notícias, mas cada dia tem 24 horas, e de alguma forma elas sempre se preenchem. Abandonei a ideia de que haverá um momento da minha vida em que não terei nada na agenda. Se um descanso acontecer, será porque eu fiz um esforço para esvaziar minha agenda, não porque por algum acaso aleatório um dia eu não tenha nenhuma tarefa.

“Deus nunca me dará mais do que posso suportar.” Deus prometeu muitas coisas. Prometeu que, quando houver tentação, Ele nos dará uma oportunidade de escapar dela (1 Coríntios 10:13). Também prometeu que nunca nos deixará nem nos desamparará (Hebreus 13:5). Em nenhum lugar das Escrituras leio que Deus nos protegerá de sobrecarregar nossas vidas. Ele simplesmente prometeu que nos dará oportunidade de tomar um caminho diferente e caminhará ao nosso lado nessa jornada.

Tantas vezes o fardo pesado que carregamos deve‑se ao fato de que outras pessoas, ou mesmo nós mesmos, colocamos coisas demais em nossa lista de tarefas. Suponha que eu escolha colocar muitos pacientes na minha agenda e esteja me sentindo exausto. Nesse caso, é hora de eu assumir responsabilidade pelo que fiz, em vez de reivindicar uma promessa mítica de que Deus me impedirá de me sobrecarregar.

“Todas essas são coisas boas que estou fazendo.” Médicos enfrentam isso muito. Queremos encaixar mais um paciente na agenda e ficar um pouco mais tarde para responder a outra mensagem porque nos sentimos responsáveis. Detestamos pensar que alguém possa precisar ir ao pronto‑socorro porque não o atendemos quando precisava de ajuda.

Só porque as coisas na sua agenda são “coisas boas” que beneficiam outras pessoas e edificam o reino, não significa que você não precise reduzir em uma área ou outra. Se está se sentindo esgotado emocionalmente, provavelmente é hora de remover alguns itens da sua lista de afazeres.

Conclusão

Há outras coisas que poderiam ser mencionadas. Ter apoio de alguém, meditar nas Escrituras e até tirar férias são todas coisas que podem ajudar.

Quando leio sobre alguns dos pregadores famosos do passado, vejo em algumas de suas vidas uma montanha‑russa. Eles se forçavam ao máximo, envolviam‑se em grande número de projetos e então tinham um colapso emocional. Tiravam um tempo de folga e, um mês ou dois depois, voltavam às mesmas atividades. Esse ciclo continuou durante todo o ministério deles.

Jesus nos diz que o seu jugo é suave e o seu fardo é leve (Mat. 11:28-30). Se estamos no ponto da exaustão, precisamos considerar se temos o jugo de Jesus ou se estamos trabalhando sob o fardo da nossa própria criação.

Jesus conhece nossas limitações. Ele quer que tenhamos equilíbrio, vivendo de maneira que tenhamos força não apenas para hoje, mas também para amanhã, para a próxima semana e para o próximo ano – até que Ele venha novamente.

"O give thanks unto the God of heaven: for His mercy endureth for ever"
—Psalm 136:26

In your journey of life, from infancy to where you are today, have you ever taken a few minutes to meditate on the mercy God has shown you? Infancy to childhood, childhood to youth, youth to adulthood, and beyond, God's everlasting mercy is upon them that fear Him! The scripture says in Deuteronomy 7:9 that the mercy of God extends way past our short lives here on earth, even to a thousand generations. Take a moment and wonder in the glory and beauty of this unchanging, eternal attribute of God!

As we take a look at the history behind this hymn, let us endeavor to see the hand of God at work in the life of the hymn writer. The hymn, "When All Thy Mercies O My God," written in 1712, has been published in 994 hymnals and is to this day in the list of the best 100 hymns ever written. As the writer nears the end of his time on earth, he reflects in this hymn his awe at the mercies of God toward him throughout his life.

Joseph Addison, born May 1, 1672, was an English essayist, poet, and man of letters. Concerning his birth, we find that he “appeared weak and unlikely to live", Mr. Tyers says.* And that “he was laid out for dead as soon as he was born.” Without doubt, the providence of God preserved his young life and gave him nearly half a century to serve Him on the earth. He was the eldest son of Lancelot Addison, a well-learned man and minister in his church. His father, being a studious man himself, made sure his son Joseph had a good education. He commenced his studies in his hometown of Milston, in Wiltshire, England.

While in school around 1685, the 13-year-old hymn writer met and became best of friends with Richard Steele, the two of them being only a few months apart in age. They continued their friendship throughout the years, and 27 years later from 1711 to 1712, they cofounded The Spectator magazine, in which this hymn was first published.

After passing through several schools, Addison went to Oxford when he was about 15 years old. While he was there, he continued to gain in learning and skill, especially in the areas of writing Latin poems and essays. By the time he was 22, in 1694, he also began to show his skill at writing English poetry.

One of the most notable details of his life that conveyed to him the mercy of God is how he managed to narrowly escape an awful shipwreck. It was this tragedy and his frightening tale of survival that would go on to inspire the writing of this uplifting hymn.

Here is the hymn with the original 13 verses:

When all Thy mercies, O my God,
My rising soul surveys,
Transported with the view,
I’m lost In wonder, love and praise.

Thy Providence my life sustained,
And all my wants redressed,
While in the silent womb I lay,
And hung upon the breast.

To all my weak complaints and cries
Thy mercy lent an ear,
Ere yet my feeble thoughts had learned,
To form themselves in prayer.

Unnumbered comforts to my soul
Thy tender care bestowed,
Before my infant heart conceived
From Whom those comforts flowed.

When in the slippery paths of youth
With heedless steps I ran,
Thine arm unseen conveyed me safe,
And led me up to man.

Through hidden dangers, toils, and deaths,
It gently cleared my way;
And through the pleasing snares of vice,
More to be feared than they.

O how shall words with equal warmth
The gratitude declare,
That glows within my ravished heart?
But thou canst read it there.

Thy bounteous hand with worldly bliss
Hath made my cup run o’er;
And, in a kind and faithful Friend,
Hath doubled all my store.

Ten thousand thousand precious gifts
My daily thanks employ;
Nor is the last a cheerful heart
That tastes those gifts with joy.

When worn with sickness, oft hast Thou
With health renewed my face;
And, when in sins and sorrows sunk,
Revived my soul with grace.

Through every period of my life
Thy goodness I’ll pursue
And after death, in distant worlds,
The glorious theme renew.

When nature fails, and day and night
Divide Thy works no more,
My ever grateful heart,
O Lord,Thy mercy shall adore.

Through all eternity to Thee
A joyful song I’ll raise;
For, oh, eternity’s too short
To utter all Thy praise!

As we endeavor to understand the life and story of the hymnologist, let's take a short look at some disappointments he faced. Being single into his 40s, he had hopes of someday having a happy marriage. His marriage to Charlotte, a widow of 15 years, didn’t turn out as he had anticipated. It is said that their courtship was long and anxious. They were married in August 1716 in his 44th year. A quote states that “He is said to have first known her by becoming tutor to her son. The marriage, if uncontradicted report can be credited, made no addition to his happiness; it neither found them nor made them equal."* In addition to his less-than-ideal marriage, the loss of his good friend Richard Steele sometime after that took a toll on him.

By the year 1717, his health began to decline rapidly, and by March 1718, he had to resign some of his work positions, having a great need for rest and quietness. "The disease under which Addison laboured appears to have been asthma. It became more violent after his retirement from office and was now accompanied by dropsy. His deathbed was placid and resigned, and comforted by those religious hopes which he had so often suggested to others..." *

One last note I will include here on the life of the hymn writer is the account of his passing. There was a young man by the name of Lord Warwick, rough and loose in character, who Addison had often tried to win to the faith, all to no avail. Nearing the end of his life, he endeavored one last attempt to impress this young man with the importance of Christianity. He sent for him to come and be present as he passed away, saying, "I have sent for you that you may see how a Christian can die." We have no record of how this experience affected Warwick’s behavior, but we can assume that it most likely did. Joseph Addison died at Holland House on the 17th of June, 1719, six weeks after his 47th birthday. He is buried in the Poet's Corner of Westminster Abbey.

This hymn has several tunes: “St Peter,” composed by Alexander Robert Reinagle in 1836, is used in the Church Hymnal and Christian Hymnary. The tune "Geneva" was composed by John Cole in 1805. He was born in Tewksbury, England, and came to the United States in his boyhood. Baltimore, Maryland became his American home, and he was educated there. Early in life, he became a musician and music publisher. He continued to compose music until his death. This tune is found in the Zion's Praises, Hymns of the Church, and Harmonia Sacra. The tune "Contemplation", composed by F.A.Gore Ouseley, is more widely used by evangelical and other church groups. Other hymns by Joseph Addison include "The Lord my Pasture Shall Prepare" and "The Spacious Firmament." Here is one final quote to help us understand who Joseph Addison was and what he believed. "His religion has nothing in it enthusiastic or superstitious; he appears neither weakly credulous nor wantonly skeptical; his morality is neither dangerously lax nor impracticably rigid. All the enchantment of fancy and all the cogency of argument are employed to recommend to the reader his real interest, the care of pleasing the Author of his being."
